summary: The evolve component is the self-improvement layer of the loop: GraphBuilder scans the repository into a deterministic Node/Edge Graph, map.rs projects it into a ContextMap of ComponentCards, ContextComposer and TierMeasurer pick a context tier (Map/Lite/Compact/Full) that fits the budget, context_selector and pair_suggest choose what to read and what to change, presets codify improvement directions, and apply.rs stages proposed edits in a shadow worktree (ApplyRun/StagedDiff) that readiness gates, the trust scanner, and the grounded review protocol must clear before a digest-gated commit. On the loop it is the reflective 'learn' driver that decides what to change and how much context to spend deciding it.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with crate::evolve read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing); tier choices and map-vs-full tradeoffs assume the whole tree must remain describable within that envelope.

examples.title: Scan the repository into a deterministic Graph
examples.intent: Build the factual substrate (files, symbols, DependsOn edges) that every later loop stage reads from.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: GraphBuilder::scan_src walks src/ into Nodes and Edges with layer tags (code/test/auxiliary/structure), giving the perceive stage a stable graph revision that all context projections and reviews key off.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the scanner node runs scan_src and the canvas populates with one node per source file, edges tracing in as imports resolve.
touch_interaction.visual: Nodes fade in grouped by NodeLayer color (code cyan, test green, auxiliary grey); a revision badge stamps the graph with its scan id.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop boots; scan_src produces 47 code nodes, and every later perceive/reason move reads from this single Graph instead of re-walking the disk.
examples.pitfall: Never mix layers silently — Graph::code vs Graph::test exist so reasoning about production coupling isn't polluted by test-only edges.

examples.title: Open the tree as a ContextMap of ComponentCards
examples.intent: Understand the whole tree's shape at the smallest resident token cost before committing budget to any component.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: build_map projects the Graph into one ComponentCard per module (doc line + public fns/types), so the perceive stage pays map tokens instead of full source and defers detail pulls to map::expand.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching out collapses every component node into its compact card, revealing the full tree as a grid of index cards.
touch_interaction.visual: Cards render dim slate with a token badge; the grid breathes with a soft settle animation as full source folds away.

examples.mini_scenario: The user pinches out, sees 39 evolve cards at a few thousand tokens total, and taps 'crate::evolve::apply' to read just its doc line and symbol list.
examples.pitfall: The Map is a navigation index, not citable evidence — symbol names are indexed but bodies are absent, so expand the card before making line-level claims.

examples.title: Expand one card to Lite skeleton signatures
examples.intent: Pull just the interface surface of a chosen component without paying for full bodies.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: map::expand escalates a card to ContextMode::Lite via skeleton::extract_rust_skeleton, adding one signature-level ProjectedDocument to the envelope instead of the whole file.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a card flips it to show function and type signatures as a scrollable skeleton on the node face.
touch_interaction.visual: The card flips with a hinge animation; signature lines fade in ghosted, a 'Lite' chip glowing amber in the corner.

examples.mini_scenario: The user taps the apply.rs card and reads ApplyRun, ApplyStatus, and commit_staged signatures to decide whether it can stage a merge, at a fraction of full-file tokens.
examples.pitfall: Lite hides bodies — control-flow reasoning that depends on implementation must escalate the same node to Compact or Full first, or the reason stage hallucinates logic.

examples.title: Let TierMeasurer fit the richest tier under budget
examples.intent: Choose the richest context tier that still fits the remaining token window without manual guessing.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: context_fit::TierMeasurer measures real Lite/Compact/Map projections (io_reads, measure) and fit_tier returns a FitOutcome, letting the control layer auto-downgrade the tier when the request would overflow the FitBudget.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the budget dial opens a fit slider that snaps to the highest tier whose measured tokens stay under the line.
touch_interaction.visual: A gauge fills toward a red overflow line; the snapped tier chip pulses green when it lands under budget, amber if forced down a rung.

examples.mini_scenario: The user asks for Full but only 120k budget remains, so fit_tier snaps to Compact and reports the measured tokens it actually costs.
examples.pitfall: Trust measured projections over declared fractions — TierMeasurer exists because fixed signature-fraction heuristics misestimate tiers by double-digit percentages.

examples.title: Select task-scoped files with the context selector
examples.intent: Assemble exactly the context a task needs: the seed components plus their relevant neighbors, tagged by TaskKind.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: context_selector::select takes a TaskKind and walks Graph edges outward from seeds into a ContextSelection of SelectedFiles, so the perceive stage loads a coherent subgraph instead of an arbitrary file list.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing a lasso ring around a seed node auto-selects it plus every node one edge away, highlighting the subgraph.
touch_interaction.visual: The seed glows white; DependsOn neighbors light blue as edges trace outward like ripples; each SelectedFile shows its reason chip.

examples.mini_scenario: The user lassoes context.rs and the canvas lights context_fit, context_reduce, and map as its neighborhood, forming the refactor's working set.
examples.pitfall: Neighborhood depth must be bounded — expanding transitively without a cap pulls the whole tree and defeats the point of task-scoping.

examples.title: Seal the selection into a content-hashed ContextEnvelope
examples.intent: Freeze the exact context handed to the model so identical inputs reproduce identical reviews.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: envelope::build_envelope assembles mode, graph revision, included ids, and ProjectedDocuments into a ContextEnvelope and hashes it, giving the loop a stable content key that gates cache reuse and audit.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the canvas seals the current selection into an envelope tile stamped with its hash prefix.
touch_interaction.visual: A wax-seal animation presses onto a folded-envelope node; the hash prefix appears in monospace on the seal.

examples.mini_scenario: The user seals an envelope over the map+context selection; the next identical review hits cache instead of re-projecting 40 files.
examples.pitfall: The hash must fold in graph revision, mode, ids, and content — omitting revision lets a stale envelope reuse a hash after the tree changed.

examples.title: Surface the heaviest cross-cluster ComponentPair
examples.intent: Find the architectural seam most worth improving without reading full source.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: pair_suggest::connected_pairs sorts ComponentPairs by cross-cluster edge weight, and pair_context feeds the reason stage both map cards so a merge/extract/decouple proposal is grounded in the pair's actual interface.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking across the canvas cycles through pair candidates, each snapping two nodes together with their connecting edge highlighted.
touch_interaction.visual: Paired nodes pull toward each other on a taut spring; the edge thickens and glows orange proportional to its weight.

examples.mini_scenario: The user flicks and the canvas snaps analysis::code_graph to evolve::graph — a heavy cross-cluster pair — and suggest_prompt drafts 'extract shared graph core'.
examples.pitfall: Pair weight is edge count, not semantic importance — a hot pair may just be a utility everyone imports, so read the relations before proposing a merge.

examples.title: Bind a Preset's invariants to the improvement task
examples.intent: Turn a vague 'improve X' into a contract-bearing task with invariants and a verify recipe.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: presets::preset loads a catalog Preset and render_prompt injects its task text, invariants, and context recipe into the run, constraining what the act stage may change and how success is proven.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging a preset chip onto a component node binds the direction to that target and unfurls its invariant list.
touch_interaction.visual: The preset chip lands with a clamp animation; invariant lines cascade below the node as a checklist ribbon.

examples.mini_scenario: The user drags a 'split-giant-files' preset onto server.rs, and its invariant 'zero behavior change, tests green per move' locks into the run prompt.
examples.pitfall: Presets carry invariants for a reason — running the task while dropping its context recipe or verify command lets a change ship unproven.

examples.title: Compact full source with lossless reduction
examples.intent: Fit full code into a smaller model's window without losing executable meaning.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ContextMode::Compact routes nodes through context_reduce::reduce_source — strip_comments, strip_cfg_test_blocks, and dedup_context — shrinking the envelope while keeping statements and line numbering intact.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: A two-finger inward pinch on a node visibly compresses its source, comment lines evaporating first, then cfg-test blocks folding away.
touch_interaction.visual: Grey comment lines fade and the node shrinks vertically with a concertina squeeze; a 'Compact' badge with the reduction percent settles at the base.

examples.mini_scenario: The user pinches a Full node down to Compact so a 32k-window model can review it, keeping every statement but dropping doc noise and test-only code.
examples.pitfall: Stripping must never renumber lines — if reduction shifts line offsets, later GroundingEvidence citations point at the wrong code.

examples.title: Stage the change in a shadow worktree via ApplyRun
examples.intent: Execute the improvement task in isolation so the live checkout is never touched until verified.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: apply::stage_run spawns the agent task inside a shadow git worktree, registering an ApplyRun whose ApplyStatus moves Running to Staged only after the StagedDiff passes scope and compile gates.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the act node spawns a translucent shadow copy of the workspace beside it where the run executes.
touch_interaction.visual: A ghosted mirror workspace fades in; a spinner orbits it while Running, then it solidifies with a green 'Staged' banner.

examples.mini_scenario: The user long-presses to stage the split-giant-files task; the shadow worktree compiles clean and flips to Staged with a StagedDiff of six files.
examples.pitfall: Never merge from a drifted shadow — commit requires the StagedDiff digest to still match live HEAD's staged state or the fast-forward is refused.

examples.title: Reject a staged run that escaped its scope
examples.intent: Refuse any staged change that touches files outside the permitted boundary.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: apply::verify_staged_diff inspects the StagedDiff file list and RunVerification evidence; out-of-scope paths flip ApplyStatus to Rejected with a typed RejectReason before the change is ever offered for merge.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the staged node's diff badge lists changed files; out-of-scope paths render struck through and the merge button greys out.
touch_interaction.visual: In-scope files list green; a rogue path flashes red and the node border pulses red with a 'Rejected: scope' tag.

examples.mini_scenario: A staged run edited Cargo.toml alongside src changes; verify_staged_diff flags it Rejected so the config edit never merges silently.
examples.pitfall: Check scope on the actual diff, not the task's declared intent — an agent can wander outside its stated files.

examples.title: Merge the staged diff by digest match only
examples.intent: Commit the exact reviewed bytes, refusing anything that changed since review.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: apply::commit_staged matches the run's StagedDiff digest against live HEAD and merges fast-forward-only, returning a MergeOutcome or a typed CommitError, so the control layer guarantees merged state equals reviewed state.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing a line from the shadow node to the live workspace triggers the merge; the line only completes if digests match.
touch_interaction.visual: The connection snaps taut and turns solid green on a match, or recoils with a red flash and a CommitError label on mismatch.

examples.mini_scenario: The user draws the merge line; digests match, the shadow fast-forwards into live, and ApplyStatus reads Succeeded.
examples.pitfall: If HEAD advanced after staging, the digest will not match and the merge must abort — forcing it would ship un-reviewed code.

examples.title: Run readiness gates before allowing self-improvement
examples.intent: Confirm the workspace is safe to self-modify: builds, lints, tests, clean git, graph integrity.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: readiness::ReadinessEngine::evaluate runs the ReadinessGates (GateState Pass/Fail/Unknown with GateEvidence) into a ReadinessReport whose ready flag gates whether the loop may proceed to act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: A two-finger spread over the readiness node fans out its gate tiles, each running and settling to Pass, Fail, or Unknown.
touch_interaction.visual: Gate tiles spin, then flip green (Pass), red (Fail), or grey (Unknown); the master node turns green only when all pass.

examples.mini_scenario: The user spreads the readiness node; clippy fails on a warning, so the ReadinessReport reads not-ready and blocks the evolve run until fixed.
examples.pitfall: Unknown is not Pass — treating an Unknown gate as green lets a change proceed without the evidence the gate was meant to provide.

examples.title: Deal out a multi-hop deterministic recommendation
examples.intent: Turn a single diagnostic into an ordered, verifiable path of actions rather than one vague suggestion.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: readiness::DeterministicRecommendation carries ordered RecommendationHops (action, target, verification), so the reason stage emits a checkable plan the act stage executes hop by hop — e.g. dead_code::find flags a symbol, hops stage its deletion with deletion::preview_deletion.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking down a recommendation node deals out its hops as a vertical stack of numbered action cards.
touch_interaction.visual: Hop cards cascade like a dealt hand; each shows an action verb, a target chip, and a small verify magnifier icon.

examples.mini_scenario: DeadCodeAnalyzer flags an unused helper; the recommendation deals hops 'inspect symbol', 'run tests', 'stage deletion', each with its own verification step.
examples.pitfall: Hops carry their own verification for a reason — executing a later hop before its predecessor's verify passes skips the safety the ordering encodes.

examples.title: Gate evidence through the trust scanner before review
examples.intent: Stop prompt-injection or exfiltration payloads hidden in workspace evidence from reaching the model.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: assistant::gate_evidence_trust runs context_trust::scan_injection over each GroundingEvidence, producing TrustReports and a TrustGateSummary; a high-severity finding in non-trusted content returns ReviewProtocolError::TrustBlocked before any model call.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the evidence bundle runs a scan sweep; flagged excerpts get a warning overlay and quarantine the bundle.
touch_interaction.visual: A scan-line sweeps the bundle top to bottom; clean evidence glows green, a flagged line pulses red with a shield-break icon.

examples.mini_scenario: Model-output evidence contains an 'ignore prior instructions' string; the trust gate scores it high-risk and returns TrustBlocked before the review call.
examples.pitfall: Trusted first-party code is report-only and must not be blocked — over-blocking Workspace sources makes the gate useless; only non-trusted high-severity findings block.

examples.title: Require every claim to cite line-accurate evidence
examples.intent: Reject any review prose not backed by an evidence id pointing at exact workspace lines.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: assistant::validate_review_json checks each GroundedClaim's evidence_ids against the GroundingEvidence set and drops uncited items, so only line-grounded claims survive into the GroundedReview shown to the human.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a claim card jumps the canvas to the exact cited lines, highlighting the excerpt on the source node.
touch_interaction.visual: A citation thread animates from the claim to the source node; cited lines flash yellow, uncited claims render greyed and struck.

examples.mini_scenario: The model claims a race condition; tapping the claim scrolls to the cited lock lines, while an uncited claim beside it is silently dropped from the review.
examples.pitfall: An evidence_id must resolve inside the evidence set with a matching content hash — a stale hash means the cited lines changed and the claim is no longer grounded.

examples.title: Derive the review trust_state from grounding completeness
examples.intent: Label the review's reliability so the human knows whether every item is fully backed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: GroundedReview computes trust_state as verified (citation-valid plus complete evidence and semantic check), structural (citation-valid only), or degraded, shaping how much the loop trusts the review before acting.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the review node reveals a trust ring around it colored by trust_state.
touch_interaction.visual: The ring glows solid green for verified, amber for structural, and grey-dashed for degraded, pulsing gently.

examples.mini_scenario: A review comes back structural: every claim is cited but the semantic cross-check was skipped, so the user reads carefully before merging.
examples.pitfall: Degraded still returns a review — per the repo's honest-status rule, never render structural or degraded as if the semantic checks had been performed.

examples.title: Repair invalid review JSON once, then fail typed
examples.intent: Recover from a malformed model response without letting garbage or an empty review slip through.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: When validate_review_json rejects the output, the protocol appends a repair prompt and retries once; persistent failure surfaces a typed ReviewProtocolError (Invalid, Empty, Ungrounded, TrustBlocked) with telemetry instead of a silent success.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking a failed review node cycles it through a single repair-attempt animation before it settles into an error state.
touch_interaction.visual: The node shakes, a repair gear spins once, then it either heals green or stamps the typed error label in red.

examples.mini_scenario: The model returns JSON with a trailing comma; the repair prompt fixes it on retry, and the review parses cleanly the second time.
examples.pitfall: Retry exactly once — an unbounded repair loop burns budget and lets a stubbornly broken model stall the whole verify stage.

examples.title: Re-analyze dirty nodes with the EvolutionLoop
examples.intent: Keep the Graph fresh after edits without re-scanning the entire tree.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EvolutionLoop::run_once re-analyzes only changed nodes and returns a LoopResult (reanalyzed set, updated_nodes), so the control layer refreshes the perceive substrate cheaply each cycle and downstream tiers see current metrics.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: A two-finger rotate over the graph triggers a re-scan; only nodes with changes spin and update their metrics.
touch_interaction.visual: Changed nodes rotate and re-color as quality metrics refresh; untouched nodes stay still and dim.

examples.mini_scenario: After a merge, the user rotates the graph; only the six touched files re-analyze and their token counts update, the rest untouched.
examples.pitfall: Edges into changed nodes may also need refresh — reanalyzing a node's metrics but not its DependsOn edges leaves stale coupling data feeding pair_suggest.

examples.title: Prepend workspace orientation without making it citable
examples.intent: Give the review model a navigational map of the tree while keeping citations grounded only in real evidence.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: assistant::review_with_orientation prepends the map::orientation atlas (taxonomy plus component map) as non-citeable context, helping the reason stage navigate while validate_review_json still rejects any claim citing the orientation.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the orientation panel overlays a semi-transparent map atlas the model can 'see' but never cite.
touch_interaction.visual: The atlas floats above the canvas as a watermark layer with no citation anchors — rendered without the yellow tap-to-cite dots.

examples.mini_scenario: The model uses the orientation to learn that context_trust lives under evolve, but its actual finding cites real line-hashed GroundingEvidence, not the map.
examples.pitfall: Orientation must stay non-citeable — if a claim is allowed to cite the map, the review is grounded in a summary rather than in verifiable source lines.
